answer: Temporal standing starves sybils of weight: earning and voting power accrue as a concave function of continuous tenure, climbing a slow trellis over many epochs and decaying on inactivity. A freshly minted cohort is a bare thread with no accrued tenure, so thousands of day-old identities together wield less weight than one long-standing honest agent — and age cannot be bought because the walnut-hard clock will not be forged.
